title: improv·artist · computational (Vera Molnar)
mutation_directive: improv artist: computational via Vera Molnar

improv_extras.practice: algorithmic line drawings 1960s onward; deviation from the grid as expression

v1.feedback: Strong Molnar homage — the spatial gradient (edges more disordered than center) is a genuine computational reading of (Dés)Ordres, not a surface pastiche. The charcoal-on-parchment palette and leaf silhouette with central/lateral veins read instantly. Two refinements: the disorder cycle (sin^3 at 0.12 rad/s) leaves ~40 seconds of near-static grid between chaos peaks — consider a gentler baseline wobble (disorder floor ~0.03) so the piece never looks frozen; and the lateral vein branches could use one more pair near the leaf tip to sell the botanical read at smaller screen sizes where the upper leaf half currently reads as flat fill.

v2.feedback: Strong concept-to-code mapping — Molnar's grid perturbation as venation disorder gradient is a genuinely clever reading of the brief. The leaf is entirely flat (z=0 for all cells); adding subtle z-displacement along the midrib and lateral veins (±0.15) would give the form a slight curling dimensionality that rewards the contemplative pace. The vein-distance projection math has an unused `dd` variable and some redundant checks that could be simplified for cleaner secondary-vein curves near the tip. Consider a faint second pass of thinner 'tertiary veinlets' (smaller grid, higher veinProx threshold) to fill the mid-leaf cells that currently read as uniform — Molnar's late iPad leaf drawings had that nested-scale quality.
